McpServerDefinition.description: Hall of Fame and player cards of the Polyglot Arcade, rendered as HXL widgets in Claude, ChatGPT and Slackbot.

tools.descriptionOverride: Ranks the players of a Polyglot Arcade game (Block Drop, Pellet Chase, Four in a Row, Brick Breaker, Snake) by their best round, or names the champion of every game when no game is given. Optional period: today, week, month or all. Use it for questions like "Who is this week's champion?" or "Show the Brick Breaker high scores". Send exactly one object in inputs: the result renders as a widget only for a single request. To compare periods or games, call the tool once for each.

Shows a Polyglot Arcade player's personal best and rank in every game and their last five rounds. Leave the player empty for the person who asks. Use it for questions like "How am I doing in the arcade?" or "Show Ada's player card". Send exactly one object in inputs: the result renders as a widget only for a single request. For several players, call the tool once for each.

Starts a round of a Polyglot Arcade game (Block Drop, Pellet Chase, Four in a Row, Brick Breaker, Snake): shows the player's best, the champion and a button that opens the game. Leave the game empty to list every game. Use it for requests like "I want to play a round of Snake" or "What can I play?". Real-time games open in the arcade and save their round there. Four in a Row can be played in the chat with playFourInARow. Send exactly one object in inputs: the result renders as a widget only for a single request.

Plays Four in a Row against the CPU in the conversation and renders the board. Writes to the arcade: it saves the game after every move and records the score when the game ends. No column shows the current game or starts one. For a message like "Four in a Row: drop my disc in column 3 (move 5)", pass column 3 and moveNumber 5 and call the tool once. Every move needs a new call: the board only changes through this tool, so never describe a move without calling it. Set newGame to true only when the player asks for a new game; difficulty is easy or normal. Never choose a column for the player. The board in the result is complete, so answer in at most one short sentence. Send exactly one object in inputs: the result renders as a widget only for a single request.
